tagline: From a gold camp over Washington's highest pass to Lake Roosevelt.
intro: SR 20 leaves Republic along the Sanpoil River, turns up O'Brien Creek into the Kettle River Range and climbs through the Colville National Forest to Sherman Pass. It crosses in a series of hairpin turns at 5,575 feet, the highest maintained pass in Washington. Then it comes down along Sherman Creek to Lake Roosevelt, the dammed Columbia, and crosses over toward Kettle Falls.
Pine, fir and larch forest lines the way, with old logging sites among the trees.

moments.title: Republic
moments.text: The gold camp began as Eureka in 1897, but the state already had a post office of that name, so it became Republic instead.

moments.title: Stonerose Fossil Site
moments.text: An artist and a Seattle high school student found these beds in 1977, and with a permit visitors may dig leaves, insects and feathers from a lake bottom 51 million years old.

moments.title: Kettle Falls
moments.text: The first town stood on the bank of the Columbia until the lake behind Grand Coulee Dam took it in 1940, and planners moved it to Meyers Falls, by the railroad.
